# Red Groves · Book II, pp. 314–315
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	314
P	Half a day east of Stonetop is a copse of trees that turn blood red (leaves, bark, and all) at the autumnal equinox. By spring, the color has returned to normal. The <b>Forest</b> <b>Folk</b> (page 150) warned the villagers to avoid this place. They never said why.
B	An iron tang in the air
B	The scrutiny of the forest upon you, heavy like a blanket
B	Words of warning, faintly heard in the breeze, in the rustling leaves, in the insect hum and birdsong.
B	<b>Spring/Summer:</b> bright green shoots/ leaves bursting from black bark and mud
B	<b>Autumn/Winter:</b> overwhelming, glossy red <b>Tip:</b> faintly whisper things like "turn back" or "not welcome" or "go away" and then pretend you didn't say anything
H2	Lore
HR
P	<b>Something interesting:</b> A dozen such groves dot the Great Wood. Some redden in the fall, others in spring. Some, like the one near Stonetop, are large and old; others are just a few young trees.
P	<b>Something useful:</b> When you <b><i>enter a red</i></b> <b><i>grove</i></b>, you draw the forest's wrath unless…
E	you come naked and empty handed, having been ritually purified;
E	you bear a dying spirit, wishing to pass on; or
E	you are cloaked in subtle magic.
P	Redwood serves as a conduit for <b>spirits of</b> <b>the wild</b> (page 356). Some of the Forest Folks' most powerful totems are made of redwood. Alas, harvesting redwood without the permission of the forest spirits is sure to draw their primal, relentless ire.
H2	Why are they so special?
HR
P	That's for you to decide. Maybe...
E	they are where <b>spirits of the wild</b> (page 356) are born and where they come to die;
E	they each imprison some terrible evil;
E	they each mark the grave of a champion of <b>Danu</b> (page 64); or
E	it's different for each grove.
PAGE	315
H2	Hooks
HR
B	A dying <b>glasbren</b> (page 366) seeks a mortal to convey her to the Red Grove.
B	The Red Grove is corrupted by the <b>Things Below</b> (page 412). Its spirits are confused and unwell, and the Grove will soon start spawning horrors.
B	A villager steals a branch of redwood, and is cursed with the forest's wrath.
H2	Inhabitants
HR
P	Any <b>spirit of the wild</b> (page 356) might be found here, but each grove hosts at least a few <b>brennauwed</b> (page 366) and is protected by <b>coedwaig</b> (page 369). <b>Butcherbirds</b> (page 204) frequent the Groves while they are red.
HR

H3	The Forest's Wrath
P	Threat (<i>affliction</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to punish the perpetrator and those who protect them
P	The greater the transgression, the more quickly the curse escalates and the greater the penance required.
C	Nightmares, ire from beasts and birds, plants tend to wither and die
C	Friends and family are affected, too; birds and small beasts harass them in town
C	The whole village is affected; sleep is scarce, nerves frayed, the Wood is hostile
C	Saplings sprout in town overnight, or when folk aren't looking
C	<b>Impending doom</b>: Crops fail, livestock revolt, homes collapse, the granary rots
